actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is a collection of MuJoCo models of the Franka Panda ('Franka panda mujoco models')
The README says the models adjust the default joint positions, with an offset of -pi/2 on joint6 and -pi/4 on joint7
The README says the joint4 range was reduced to avoid the gimbal-lock configuration
The README says the joint limits were adjusted to avoid hitting the limits during operation with the hardware
The README credits the robot meshes and specs to franka_ros and the Franka control_parameters page
The card's first model is the MJCF scene whose root element is '<mujoco model="bi-franka_panda v200">'
The bi-franka scene includes assets/basic_scene.xml, assets/assets.xml and assets/gripper_assets.xml, and sets an empty compiler meshdir
The bi-franka scene is a torso with a leftarm that includes assets/chain0.xml and a rightarm that includes assets/chain1.xml
The bi-franka scene includes the left arm actuator set assets/actuator0.xml and the two-arm actuator set assets/actuator1.xml
The compiler angle is radian, so the joint ranges of the model are radians
The model sets an explicit option timestep of 0.002 s
The panda default class gives its position actuators ctrllimited true and forcelimited true, and the joint default is limited true with axis 0 0 1
The finger default class gives its joints damping 100 and armature 5, and its position actuators a user tuple

The left arm is seven hinge joints with ranges -2.8973 to 2.8973 (panda0_joint1), -1.7628 to 1.7628 (panda0_joint2), -2.8973 to 2.8973 (panda0_joint3), -3.0718 to -0.4 (panda0_joint4), -2.8973 to 2.8973 (panda0_joint5), -1.6573 to 2.1127 (panda0_joint6) and -2.8973 to 2.8973 (panda0_joint7)

The right arm is seven hinge joints with ranges -2.9671 to 2.9671 (panda1_joint1), -1.8326 to 1.8326 (panda1_joint2), -2.9671 to 2.9671 (panda1_joint3), -3.0718 to -0.4 (panda1_joint4), -2.9671 to 2.9671 (panda1_joint5), -1.6573 to 2.1127 (panda1_joint6) and -2.8973 to 2.8973 (panda1_joint7)
panda0_finger_joint1 and panda0_finger_joint2 are slide joints with range 0 to 0.04 m
panda1_finger_joint1 and panda1_finger_joint2 are slide joints with range 0 to 0.04 m

The left arm has seven position actuators, panda0_joint1 to panda0_joint7, with ctrlranges -2.9671 to 2.9671, -1.8326 to 1.8326, -2.9671 to 2.9671, -3.1416 to 0.0, -2.9671 to 2.9671, -1.66 to 2.1817 and -2.9671 to 2.9671

The right arm has seven position actuators, panda1_joint1 to panda1_joint7, with ctrlranges -2.9671 to 2.9671, -1.8326 to 1.8326, -2.9671 to 2.9671, -3.1416 to 0.0, -2.9671 to 2.9671, -0.0873 to 3.8223 and -0.0873 to 3.8223
The right arm's two finger joints have position actuators panda1_leftfinger and panda1_rightfinger with ctrlrange 0 to 0.04
The model declares a Franka_wrist_cam camera and an end_effector site on panda0_link7
The model's mesh assets are STL files under meshes/collision and meshes/visual, with a 1.01 scale on the dark visual meshes

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so one ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the bridge takes no seed input and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the served scene for 18 one-DOF joints, 16 actuator ctrlranges and the 2 ms time step, then moves each actuated joint toward its control value; it computes no inertia, torque, contact, equality or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the stand-in loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact: the STL meshes of assets/assets.xml:16-38 are not read, and no collision, friction or contact force is modelled

the bridge bounds ctrl by each actuator's ctrlrange, and several ctrlranges are wider than the joint range (for example panda0_joint1 at assets/actuator0.xml:11 against assets/chain0.xml:16); the fake does not enforce joint limits, while MuJoCo stops a joint at its range

the left gripper has no actuator: assets/actuator0.xml declares only the seven left arm actuators, so the two left finger joints (assets/chain0.xml:62-88) are unactuated; only the right finger joints have the two position actuators of assets/actuator1.xml:17-18
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine; the sim path that imports the real mujoco was not run
snapshot and restore use the stand-in's own integration state (time, qpos, qvel, ctrl), not mjSTATE_INTEGRATION of the engine, so a snapshot is exact only inside the stand-in
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the Franka_wrist_cam camera and the joint sensors of assets/assets.xml are not exposed, and only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is published
no physical Franka robot is modelled and nothing was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the integration state stays readable
